- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 75–80+), then correct downward — model fails to adjust quickly enough.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted: model holds high values too long after peaks, ignoring the tendency to revert to prior 30-day average.
- Forecast bias is often upward in the first 10 days, then downward — model exhibits a “lagged” correction pattern.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the last 5–7 days of history, leading to overestimation of true values in the final 10–15 days.
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the first 5–7 days after a new low, failing to recognize the “recovery lag” from recent dips.
